text:
Mira: Aurora POC kicks off Monday. They asked for a single-run playbook showing how we issue hosted API keys for two devs, how rotation works, and how to run an immediate revoke test. Can we compile a short handoff? cc @sam_se @toni_sre @jorn_security
Sam_SE: Short answer: ephemeral scoped keys + one-time delivery link + rotate API + revoke CLI. How long will Aurora need access?
Mira: 12 days. They
 like automatic rotation every 24h but want to be able to force revoke during tests. Security insists on audit export to their S3.
Toni_SRE: Proposed playbook (minimal):
1) Create two ephemeral keys with 24h TTL, limited scopes (generate, embeddings).
2) Deliver via one-time signed link (15m) or push to their secret store (AWS Secrets Manager / 1Password).
3) Configure per-key IP allowlist if they supply CIDRs and set per-key quotas.
4) Enable audit export to Aurora's S3 (KMS-encrypted) for the POC window.
5) Provide rotate-lambda snippet they can wire into CI to call our rotate endpoint and push secrets to their vault.
6) Revoke test procedure: provision keys -> run traffic -> we revoke -> confirm 401s and audit entry.
Sam_SE: CLI/API snippets to hand them:
```
# create ephemeral key
redwood-cli keys create --type ephemeral --expires-in 24h --scopes generate,embed --note "aurora-poc-dev1"

# rotate programmatically
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/:alias/rotate

# revoke instantly
redwood-cli keys revoke <key-id>
```
Jorn_Security: Security checklist to include in the playbook: TTL <=24h (48h allowed with approval), one-time delivery or direct vault push, audit log export to customer S3 with retention window, revocation SLA (immediate from control plane; client may see in-flight requests), principle of least privilege on scopes, IP allowlist where feasible, and prohibition on embedding keys in client-side apps. Add incident contact: security@redwood.ai.
Mira: Aurora specifically asked if Redwood can host the rotation job so they don't have to run cron. Is that doable?
Toni_SRE: We can offer a managed rotation webhook for POCs: we create a service account for Aurora with permission to call rotate; they provide a target secret store endpoint and we push rotated keys there on a schedule. Alternatively we hand them a tiny lambda + IAM policy. Which do they prefer?
Mira: They prefer managed if possible. I'll check and get back.
Sam_SE: Note for the revoke test: advise them to disable aggressive socket reuse during the test and set their client to honor 401s immediately. There can be a short window of in-flight requests that succeed due to keep-alive connections. We'll document that.
Jorn_Security: Also include a short section for the security questionnaire: answer fields for token lifecycle, rotation cadence, programmatic rotate/revoke endpoints, audit export path, KMS usage, and POC contractual clause requiring rotation every 24-48h and immediate reporting on suspected compromise.
Infra-bot: Internal docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/keys/ephemeral (CLI, API, rotate lambda sample, audit export instructions).
Mira: Great. I'll assemble a one-page playbook (handoff checklist + revoke test steps + SecQ answers) and post here for review. Sam, can you pre-provision labels for the two keys so I can give names to Aurora devs when they confirm?
Sam_SE: Yep. I'll pre-create aliases aurora-poc-dev1 and aurora-poc-dev2 and leave them in pending create state. Once Mira confirms names and CIDRs I'll finalize and generate one-time links.
Toni_SRE: I'll draft the managed-rotation option terms (what we store, rotation windows, and S3 push consent) and attach the tiny Lambda example if they want to self-host.
Mira: Thanks all 44d I'll post the playbook later today and loop in Aurora infra.
Jorn_Security: I'll review the SecQ answers when you post. :lock:
